correctness.rationale: For every plane conic (including degenerate limits), its degree-4 squared ideal has rank 14. The 8-dimensional conic parameter bundle yields a 21-dimensional irreducible incidence. Bertini and uniqueness of the singular conic give generic degree one. A three-step filtration gives c(E) and s(E), the projective-bundle pushforward gives 579040-4*139412+6*22992-4*1981=151420, and a 24-fixed-point torus localization reproduces 151420 independently. No finite experiment is used to prove the geometric genericity.

originality.rationale: No reviewed primary source or indexed research record supplies the projective degree 151420 of the 21-dimensional conic-double quartic locus. Slavov gives the general singular-support moduli construction, Ducat/Urabe give its geometric family, Carmeli–Radzivilovsky give the different singular-line enumeration, and Kazarian–Kerner–Némethi treat transverse-discriminant classes along fixed loci. A genuinely new Segre integral over the conic Hilbert bundle is required; classical unindexed priority remains a stated residual risk.
residual_risks: Older unindexed enumerations of quartics with double conic, particularly Segre/Jessop, might have implicitly or explicitly calculated the same number.
The complete text of arXiv:1308.6045 was not inspected; the abstract alone cannot prove it excludes an implicit enumerative specialization.
Searches are evidence of non-coverage by checked sources, not a mathematical proof of historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: The parameter-space degree counts quartic surfaces with an unspecified double plane conic through 21 general points, a natural classical enumerative-geometric question adjacent to established line-supported counts. It is an exact invariant of a natural irreducible locus of nonnormal quartics, not a narrow unmotivated slice; its evaluation requires an eight-dimensional intersection calculation.
